image:image.image:title: The strange mercy of death
image:image.image:caption: The strange mercy of death, an essay by Michael Wargr.

image:image.image:title: The strange mercy of death social card
image:image.image:caption: I was fifteen when death moved out of the distance and into the bed beside me, and it took years before I stopped seeing it as an enemy.

image:image.image:title: The whore of Babylon was always us
image:image.image:caption: The whore of Babylon was always us, an essay by Michael Wargr.

image:image.image:title: The whore of Babylon was always us social card
image:image.image:caption: I thought religion was a trick for gullible people. Then the old stories started looking less like superstition and more like a report on the crowd, and on me.

image:image.image:title: The side effect of knowing yourself
image:image.image:caption: The side effect of knowing yourself, an essay by Michael Wargr.

image:image.image:title: The side effect of knowing yourself social card
image:image.image:caption: The most confident people I have known never seem particularly interested in the question of how they look. That, it turns out, is the trick.
